title: China's Last Shangri-La: a 2-Week Gold Window at 3,900 m | China Travel Expert
description:
Time the drive to Daocheng Yading wrong and you lose the whole reason to go: the golden larch only lasts about two weeks, in late October.

Yading, deep in western Sichuan, is nicknamed "the last Shangri-La." Its larch and poplar forests turn gold for a short window — roughly the last week of October into early November, varying year to year with the cold. Two things raise the stakes: it's high (the park shuttle drops you near 3,900 m, and the peaks climb past 6,000 m), and you can't drive your own car in — it's park shuttles only to the trailheads. October nights swing from about 5°C down below freezing. Come a week late and the valleys are already bare and brown.

🧭 Expert Tip: aim for the last week of October, and sleep a night in Daocheng town (around 3,750 m) to acclimatise before you head up — rushing straight to altitude is how trips get cut short.

稻城亚丁，中国最后的香格里拉——金黄的落叶松只美约两周，十月底最好；海拔高、只能坐景区观光车，来晚了就只剩光秃山谷。
